newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - April 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - April 11.

text.p: Telstra sues Telecom for $100m: Telecom says Telstra overcharged: Australian telecommunications giant Telstra has taken PacStar, Telecom NZ's Australian arm, to court to recover an estimated $100 million in alleged bad debts. Page 1.

SFO re-opens Bank of NZ investigation: As the State Services Commission confirmed on Thursday that Serious Fraud Office director Chas Sturt had been stood down from his job through ill health, the SFO revealed it had re-opened its inquiry into the Bank of New Zealand. Page 1.
Wine war rips along Dry River Road: A fight of Champagne proportions has broken out in Martinborough, one of the country's most toasted wine regions. Page 1.

Only face-to-face talks can solve CHH's Chilean row: Inability to negotiate directly with the head of Chile's powerful Angelini family is a key stumbling block in Carter Holt Harvey's dispute with its Chilean joint venture partner, CHH chief executive John Faraci said this week. Page 3.

Whistle blown on winebox whistleblower: Behind the scenes at the winebox Commission of Inquiry, a row has developed over four, hitherto-secret interviews done by commissioner Sir Ron Davison in April 1995. Page 3.

PM's advisor loses dough in bakery, sues Price Waterhouse: David Kirk, former All Black and adviser to Prime Minister Jim Bolger, on Thursday told the High Court at Wellington that trusting rugby colleague David Gray led to him losing $789,893 on an ill-fated bakery investment. Page 6.
Trans Tasman Properties issues prospectus for A$305 float: Trans Tasman Properties this week released the long-awaited prospectus for the A$305 million float of its Australian assets. Page 6.

Aussie managers take helm at St Lukes Group: St Lukes Group's $700 million NZ shopping centre portfolio is to be managed and developed by Australian-listed shopping mall developer, Westfield Holdings. Page 7.

Colonial Mutual wins case v brokers: Financial services company Colonial Mutual last week won resounding victories in the High Court at Wellington against two Auckland-based insurance brokers, John Handley of Lindale Financial Services and Alan Lambourne of Jason Investments. Page 7.

Blue Star revamps book retail and video-conference markets: London Bookshops has amalgamated with Whitcoulls under the Blue Star Consumer Retailing banner. The structural change came into effect at the end of March. Page 7.
NZ ready for Beijing military link: New Zealand will appoint a defence attache to China, whose three million-strong People's Liberation Army is the world's biggest military force. Page 10.
Internet row sparks call for cyber 'bill of rights': A key multimedia association, INZ, has called for a cyber "bill of rights" to guarantee the legal title of Internet domain names. Page 11.

Ducks no longer suck as Asians push egg prices up: Duck eggs, once virtually given away by egg producers, are now fetching higher prices than hen eggs as suppliers try to keep up with the demand from the local Asian market. Page 11.

Supermarkets ponder shelf space as liquor reform nears: Supermarkets won't necessarily be clamouring to take on liquor wholesalers should MPs vote to adopt the highly liberal recommendations of the liquor law review committee. Page 13.
